div.head: Hn 70.10
div.ab: Si quis de [q]uolibe[t] fact[o] occidatur, omne malum occisoris pro nichilo reputatur, si homicidium fecerit contra legem; quia scilicet rectum, quod inde habiturus erat, sibi abstulit; reddet uero quem occidit, tanquam ab eo nichil passus sit.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 588 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: ‘Leiden’, sammt Anspruch auf Entgelt; vgl. 83, 3 gegen 74, 3
‘suffering’, together with the claim to recompense; cf. 83, 3 as against 74, 3
s'uo lib' fc̄s Sc; seruo liber factus Hg; seruo liber ohne factus übrige
s'uo lib' fc̄s Sc; seruo liber factus Hg; seruo liber without factus the rest
omitted in Sc Hg; nil K

Si quis de servo liber occidatur, dann 3½ Zeilen leer Rs; vermutlich also blieb der Rest von 70, 10 unvollendet oder durchstrichen (auch u. 83, 1a fehlt der Nachsatz). Factus scheint mir original, da, wäre servus der Täter, a stünde. Beginne also mit Omne neuen Satz 70, 10a, wozu vgl. Gl Busse 5a; Blutrache 14a. Hiermit fällt meine Emendation{28} fort—reputetur—reddat{24}—nil{29} Rs

Si quis de servo liber occidatur, then 3½ lines blank Rs; presumably, therefore, the rest of 70, 10 was left unfinished or was struck through (the apodosis is also missing below 83, 1a). Factus seems to me original, since, were the servus the perpetrator, a would stand there. So begin a new sentence, 70, 10a, with Omne, on which cf. Gl Busse 5a; Blutrache 14a. My emendation{28} thus falls away—reputetur—reddat{24}—nil{29} Rs

div.ab: If anyone is killed for any deed whatever, every wrong of the slain man is reckoned as nothing, if he has committed homicide against the law; because, that is, he has taken from him the right which he was going to have from it; but let him pay for the man he killed, as though he had suffered nothing from him.
